newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Dah Sing to raise HK$381 mln in shr sale.
newsitem.headline: Dah Sing to raise HK$381 mln in shr sale.

text.p: Dah Sing Financial Holdings Ltd said on Monday it planned to issue 12.04 million new shares to an Abbey National Plc unit, raising HK$381 million to grow its banking and life insurance businesses.

The shares, which represent about five percent of the company's enlarged share, would be priced at HK$31.68 per share, compared with Friday's closing price of HK$36.40. Trading in its shares was suspended on Monday.
Dah Sing also said in a statement that its chairman David Wong had agreed to buy six million Dah Sing shares from Mitsui Trust & Banking Co Ltd at HK$30.60 per share.

After the transactions, Wong would hold 39.71 percent of the enlarged share capital of the company compared with a current 39.18 percent and Mitsui Trust's holding would be lowered to 10.31 percent from 13.48 percent, the company said.

"We are pleased that Mitsui Trust remains as a substantial shareholder and that we will contine to maintain a good business relationship with Mitsui Trust in the future as we have done since 1988," Wong said in the statement.

"We are also delighed to welcome Abbey National...as a strategic long-term shareholder in DSFH, and hope that we will be able to build further on the relationship initiated in the joint venture in private banking announced at the end of last year," he added.
Dah Sing announced last November that it had agreed to set up a joint venture international private banking operation, D.A.H. Private Bank Ltd, with Abbey National and Hambros Bank Ltd.
Abbey National chief executive Peter Birch said, "Dah Sing and Abbey National are looking at possible areas for future co-operation in both the wholesale and retail businesses."
